headline: Marseille have no Europa League points — and are still favourites in Graz
summary: Marseille have lost both Europa League games — 1-4 at Beşiktaş and 0-1 at home to Olympiakos — and sit 32nd with 0 points. And yet the market still makes them 47.5% favourites in Graz, nearly double Sturm Graz's 26.6%. The home side won the city derby 6-1 on Sunday, but lost 0-3 at Bournemouth with only 0.37 expected goals, and are without seven players. Marseille's 5-2 win at Angers explains the favourites tag, though Hojbjerg is a doubt with a muscle strain. Over 2.75 goals is 51%.
read: Sturm Graz have just won the Graz derby 6-1 and score at home, while the goal line sits at 2.75 with over at 51.0%.

facts.fact: Marseille have lost both Europa League matches — 1-4 at Beşiktaş and 0-1 at home to Olympiakos — and have no points, sitting 32nd of 36.
facts.meaning: A third defeat leaves their league-phase campaign in real trouble with five games still to play.

facts.fact: Marseille are the clear favourites at 47.5% to win, nearly double Sturm Graz's 26.6% home chance.
facts.meaning: The market still makes Marseille the side to beat, even though it gives them less than a 50-50 chance of actually winning in 90 minutes.

facts.fact: Sturm Graz beat city rivals Grazer AK 6-1 on Sunday, with a hat-trick from Oumar Diakité (reported by footmercato).
facts.meaning: They come into this one scoring freely and on a high, four days after the derby.

facts.fact: Marseille won 5-2 at Angers on Sunday, their second consecutive Ligue 1 victory.
facts.meaning: The domestic form is the reason the market keeps them as favourites despite the European record.

facts.fact: Sturm Graz are without seven players who have featured this season, including attacker S. Jatta, who has 641 minutes and two goals.
facts.meaning: The home squad is stretched in both boxes, with defender E. Soglo also out.

facts.fact: Marseille's Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg is a doubt with a muscle strain; coach Bruno Genesio said he is an option for Thursday but it is unclear whether he can start.
facts.meaning: Marseille's midfield anchor could be missing or limited, which matters against a side that has just scored six.

facts.fact: Over 2.75 goals is priced at 51.0%, with the market's fair total at 2.79.
facts.meaning: Three goals or more is seen as slightly more likely than not.

facts.fact: Sturm Graz managed only 0.37 xG in their 0-3 defeat at Bournemouth.
facts.meaning: Against a stronger European opponent they created almost nothing, a warning about the jump in level from the derby.

sources.fact: Sturm Graz beat city rivals Grazer AK 6-1 in the Austrian league, with a hat-trick from former Reims striker Oumar Diakité, going into the Marseille match.
Sturm Graz lost 3-0 away to Bournemouth in their previous Europa League match.
A Sturm Graz match was halted over the weekend when a goalkeeper suffered a serious leg injury in the derby against Grazer AK.
Austrian police have stepped up security for Sturm Graz v Marseille after violent clashes at the Graz derby against Grazer AK four days earlier, with around a thousand Marseille fans expected.
Marseille lost their first two Europa League games, 4-1 to Besiktas and 1-0 to Olympiacos, and are still without a point in the competition.
Marseille won their second consecutive league match, beating Angers 5-2, and go into the Sturm Graz game with renewed confidence.
Marseille coach Bruno Genesio said Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, returning from a strain, is an option for Thursday but it is unclear whether he can start.
Bruno Genesio has called up a young player as a surprise inclusion in the Marseille squad for the trip to Sturm Graz.
